title: The NRI's Guide to World Cup 2026 at AT&T Stadium, Dallas
excerpt: 9 matches including Argentina and a semifinal, Irving's desi food strip, DFW transit tips (there's no rail to the stadium), and how the booming DFW Indian community can attend the World Cup.
body:
Dallas is hosting more World Cup matches than any other city — 9 games at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, including Argentina matches and a semifinal. The DFW metroplex also has one of the fastest-growing Indian communities in America, centered around Irving and Plano.

Match Schedule

| Date | Match | Kickoff (CT) | |------|-------|-------------| | Sat, Jun 14 | Netherlands vs Japan | 3:00 PM | | Tue, Jun 17 | England vs Croatia | 3:00 PM | | Mon, Jun 22 | Argentina vs Austria | 12:00 PM | | Wed, Jun 25 | Japan vs Sweden | 6:00 PM | | Fri, Jun 27 | Jordan vs Argentina | 9:00 PM | | Mon, Jun 30 | Round of 32 (TBD) | TBD | | Thu, Jul 3 | Round of 32 (TBD) | TBD | | Mon, Jul 6 | Round of 16 (TBD) | TBD | | Tue, Jul 14 | Semifinal | TBD |

Where to Eat: Irving Is the DFW Desi Capital

Arlington (Near the Stadium): Annampuram on Cooper St stays open until 2 AM — Vijayawada Boneless Chicken Biryani and Ghee Masala Dosa. India Grill has the best samosas in DFW with a full bar and outdoor seating. Spicy Dhaba runs 6 PM to 2 AM for late-night dhaba-style eats.

Irving (20-30 min): The Airport Freeway strip at 535 W Airport Fwy is essentially a desi food court — Deccan Grill for Hyderabadi Dum Biryani, Shree Vimal's for Gujarati thali and dabeli, Hot N Spicy for budget-friendly butter chicken right next to India Bazaar. Bombay Sweets near the DFW Hindu Temple has jalebi and mithai that'll make you forget you're in Texas.

Richardson & Plano (30-45 min): Bawarchi has what many call the best biryani in DFW — Hyderabadi Dum Biryani and Irani Chai. Chameli does Bengali cuisine with what fans call "the best biryani in DFW, hands down." Curry Bliss has a Thursday night dosa buffet.

Getting There: The Big Challenge

There is no direct public transit to AT&T Stadium. This is the biggest logistical challenge for World Cup attendees in Dallas.

TRE Train + Free FIFA Charter Bus: Take the Trinity Railway Express from Victory Station (downtown Dallas) or Central Station (Fort Worth) to CentrePort/DFW Airport Station. From there, free FIFA charter buses run to the stadium — requires a valid World Cup match ticket. Runs 5 hours before and 3 hours after each match. Total trip: ~1.5 hours from downtown Dallas.

Rideshare: Budget $30-75 from downtown Dallas. All rideshares drop off at Arlington Esports Stadium parking lot, about a 10-minute walk. Pro tip: Wait 30 minutes after the final whistle — surge pricing drops significantly.

Driving & Parking: Starting at $128 for group stage games, purchased in advance. Premium lots run $220-740+. Expect massive traffic on I-30 and I-20 on match days.

Where to Stay

Arlington Entertainment District: Walking distance to the stadium, Texas Live! complex with restaurants and bars. Prices will be inflated during the World Cup.

Irving — Valley Ranch/Las Colinas (Best for NRIs): 20-25 min to the stadium. The cultural heart of DFW's Indian community with 50+ Indian restaurants, temples, and grocery stores within a 5-mile radius. Close to CentrePort Station for the TRE train connection.

West Plano (Coit Road): The densest concentration of Indian businesses in DFW. India Bazaar, Patel Brothers, and dozens of restaurants spanning every regional Indian cuisine. 35-45 min to the stadium.

Desi Community

DFW Hindu Temple on Westside Dr in Irving and BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir are the major temples. India Bazaar on Coit Road in Plano is a one-stop desi supermarket — think an Indian Costco. The Irving Airport Freeway corridor is the cultural heart of desi DFW.

Tickets

Available at FIFA.com/tickets. Argentina vs Austria (Jun 22) and the Semifinal (Jul 14) will command premium prices. England vs Croatia (Jun 17) is another marquee draw.
author: Diaspora Desk
